pointers.sentence: This happens as the template renders, in the tag result_list, an `InclusionAdminNode` whose function `result_list` calls `result_headers` and, for each row of the page, `items_for_result` ([The admin's templates and media](templates.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py:result_list`).

When the user has an action for the change list, `ModelAdmin.get_changelist_instance` puts `"action_checkbox"` first, the name of the method `ModelAdmin.action_checkbox`, which draws a row's checkbox ([Actions: `response_action` and `delete_selected`](actions.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_changelist_instance`).
`lookup_field` resolves a name against a row in this order (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:lookup_field`):
A field of the model; not a reverse foreign key, a generic foreign key, or a foreign key's column name such as `"home_id"` (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:_get_non_gfk_field`).

The checks refuse a reverse foreign key, and a many-to-many field, which, the documentation says, would need a query for each row ([The admin's checks: `check_dependencies` and `ModelAdminChecks`](checks.md)) (`docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).
A path is made readable itself: the header of `"home__name"` is "Home name", each underscore a space (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:label_for_field`, `django/forms/utils.py:pretty_name`).
A path is made readable itself: the header of `"home__name"` is "Home name", each underscore a space (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:label_for_field`, `django/forms/utils.py:pretty_name`).

`result_headers` makes a header a sorting link when the name is among what `BaseModelAdmin.get_sortable_by` returns: `sortable_by`, or, when that is `None` as by default, what `get_list_display` returns (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.get_sortable_by`).

A name that is not a field needs an `"admin_order_field"` on its attribute, or must be a path ending at a field; the documentation says the database does the sorting (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py:result_headers`, `docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).

A name that is not a field needs an `"admin_order_field"` on its attribute, or must be a path ending at a field; the documentation says the database does the sorting (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py:result_headers`, `docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).

`ChangeList.get_ordering_field_columns` says which columns are sorted; without `"o"` it guesses from the default ordering, since, its comment says, several columns may sort by one field (`django/contrib/admin/views/main.py:ChangeList.get_ordering_field_columns`).
`ChangeList.get_ordering_field` says what a column sorts by (`django/contrib/admin/views/main.py:ChangeList.get_ordering_field`).

`items_for_result` starts each cell from the **empty value**, what a cell shows when there is nothing to show: the model admin's `empty_value_display` if it has one, else the site's, `AdminSite.empty_value_display`, `"-"` by default (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.get_empty_value_display`); an attribute's `"empty_value_display"` replaces it for its column.
Then what `lookup_field` found decides the text (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py:items_for_result`):

Choices give their label; a boolean field an icon for yes, no or unknown; dates, times and numbers the active language's format ([Writing numbers, dates and durations](../i18n/writing-values.md)); a file or URL a link outside the linked column, a URL only if `URLValidator` accepts it, so that, the comment says, a dangerous scheme stays text (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:display_for_field`).
**Anything else**, automatic fields included: `display_for_value`, by the value's Python type, or an icon when the attribute has `"boolean"` (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:display_for_value`).
A path ending at a related model's boolean field is drawn as an icon: the path's last field, from `get_fields_from_path`, writes the cell (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
`ModelAdmin.get_list_display_links` gives the first of `list_display` when the option is empty; `None` means no links (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_list_display_links`).
`django.contrib.admin.display` sets on a function the attributes the code reads (`django/contrib/admin/decorators.py:display`).
It has no hook, and the `ChangeList` drops it in a popup (`django/contrib/admin/views/main.py:ChangeList.__init__`).
The checks require each to be an editable field, a column, and not a linked one (`django/contrib/admin/checks.py:ModelAdminChecks._check_list_editable_item`).

The inputs are a model formset over the page's rows ([Model formsets and inline formsets](../forms/model-formsets.md)), made by `ModelAdmin.get_changelist_formset` with no extra form and the form of `ModelAdmin.get_changelist_form`, whose fields `BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_dbfield` makes ([The admin's forms: `get_form` and `formfield_for_dbfield`](admin-forms.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_changelist_formset`).

On a `"GET"`, `ModelAdmin.changelist_view` makes it if the user may change the model, and `ModelAdmin._get_formset_with_permissions` takes the fields out of each form whose object `BaseModelAdmin.has_change_permission` refuses (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._get_formset_with_permissions`).

`items_for_result` draws a cell outside the linked column as its form's field whenever the name is among the form's fields, which, a comment says, lets a project vary them per request (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py:items_for_result`).
